## 2025-03-09 - XSS Vulnerability in Blog Content Rendering
**Vulnerability:** The application stores blog post content as rich HTML generated by `src/admin/BlogEditor.tsx`. In `src/admin/BlogEditor.tsx`, it was rendering unsanitized HTML via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. In `src/pages/BlogPostPage.tsx`, it was rendering this rich HTML directly as a string, which would either display raw HTML tags (broken formatting) or potentially execute scripts if converted to dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization.
**Learning:** When displaying rich HTML content generated from a WYSIWYG editor, especially when using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, the input must be sanitized to prevent Stored XSS vulnerabilities. Additionally, when providing HTML fallback strings to `DOMPurify.sanitize()` in React (e.g., inside `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`), use the standard HTML `class` attribute instead of React's `className` prop because DOMPurify parses standard HTML and will strip `className` as an invalid attribute.
**Prevention:** Always use `DOMPurify.sanitize()` when rendering user-generated or editor-generated HTML via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
